findings.text: The precedence rule the change's own docstring states - archive census first, then closure - is not pinned by any test, and inverting it leaves the whole suite green. Triggering input: archive_roles={'archived_temperature': {'HAS_UNIT': 1}} against a reconstruction closure carrying TWO HAS_UNIT edges for that identity. This is admissible - _load_archive_role_counts (signed_manifest.py:6944) refuses only when the reconstructable count is less than the archived count, never when it is greater - and it applies cleanly, because the closure-governed refusal compares its own expected 2 against live 2. Landed behaviour: {expected 1, expected_source 'archive_census', observed 2}. With the two branches of the if/elif swapped: {expected 2, expected_source 'reconstruction_closure', observed 2}, which hides the very shortfall against the archive that this field exists to surface - and both negative-control logs, the six focused tests and the full tests/standard_names run all stay green, because every landed test places a role in exactly one source. The fix is one test: a fourth case in this file asserting archive_census wins where the two sources DISAGREE. SOUND overall, not MUST-FIX, because the landed precedence is correct; what is missing is the guard that keeps it so.

Outside this node's fence, reported not fixed. The sole non-test consumer of identity_role_parity prints only expected and observed, so the field this node added is invisible at the operator surface. Answering the gate's first question with a measurement: it DOES receive None and it CANNOT fail on it - the value reaches only an f-string, and executed here against a real null row it emits 'parity archived_temperature HAS_PARENT: expected None observed 0'. The cost is reporting, not crashing, and it is now larger than before: with archive_roles={} an apply produces 35 rows per identity of which 34 read 'expected None observed 0', and the operator has no way to tell 'neither source established a count' from 'the census recorded a null'. The one-line repair is to interpolate role_counts['expected_source'] into the same line. The 67-identity restore this plan exists to perform will emit roughly 2,345 such lines.

Coverage note rather than a defect: no test in the repository asserts any CLI output line for this receipt, so the null now flowing to imas_codex/cli/sn.py:8466 is unpinned. A later change that formatted, compared or summed role_counts['expected'] would pass every gate. Pairs with the sn.py finding above and is the same fix's test.

Not a defect - the refusal-path analysis the gate asked for, recorded so it is not re-derived, and it is the answer to the second fenced question. The refusal loop is untouched by this change: it builds expected = dict.fromkeys(_ARCHIVE_EDGE_COUNTERPARTS, 0) from authority.edges - the reconstruction closure - reads live with _archive_edge_counts(..., roles=_ARCHIVE_PARITY_ROLES), then iterates expected.items(), so a role in the wider parity set but not in the counterpart registry (EVIDENCED_BY is the only one) is read and reported but never compared. Demonstrated in this reviewer's worktree: a live surplus of 5 on HAS_UNIT raises SignedManifestConflict('archive-versus-live relationship counts differ'); a live surplus of 3 on EVIDENCED_BY applies and appears in the receipt as {expected null, expected_source 'neither', observed 3}. The settled adjudication therefore holds and every archived identity that ever carried an inbound EVIDENCED_BY from a PromotionCandidate remains restorable. The known census-versus-closure split the plan already records as the successor's design call is unchanged: the receipt can still DISPLAY a shortfall against the archive that the refusal does not RAISE, and this change makes that display strictly more legible by naming which side each expectation came from.

Low severity, no in-repo consumer. SIGNED_MANIFEST_RECEIPT_SCHEMA is still 'imas-codex.signed-repair-receipt.v1' although the parity row went from {expected, observed} to {expected, expected_source, observed} and expected gained null. Any reader keying on the schema string to decide how to parse a stored receipt cannot distinguish a pre-change receipt from a post-change one. Raised because these receipts are the durable record of a 67-identity restore and are expected to outlive the code that wrote them.

justifications.durability: The three branches are each pinned by exact-dict equality and the row shape by an exhaustiveness assertion over all 35 rows, which is strong. Docked for two reachable gaps the landed tests do not construct. THE PRECEDENCE IS UNPINNED, and it is the one rule the change's docstring states normatively. No test puts a role in BOTH archived and closure with differing counts, and such an input is admissible: _load_archive_role_counts refuses only when the reconstructable count is LESS than the archived count (signed_manifest.py:6944), so archive_roles={archived_temperature: {HAS_UNIT: 1}} against a closure carrying two HAS_UNIT edges passes validation, passes the closure-governed refusal (expected 2 == live 2), and applies. Under the landed code that row reads {expected 1, archive_census, observed 2}; under a swapped precedence it reads {expected 2, reconstruction_closure, observed 2} - a receipt that no longer shows the shortfall against the archive - and the entire suite stays green. That is a silent inversion of the field's meaning on the exact case the field exists to describe. THE NULL IS UNEXERCISED AT ITS CONSUMER: no test in the repository asserts any CLI output line for this receipt (grep over tests/standard_names/test_archive_reconstruction_entry_point.py finds no parity assertion), so nothing pins that a null expected prints rather than raising, and nothing would notice if a later change started formatting or comparing it. Not a defect today - I executed the formatter against a real null row and it is safe - but the guard is absent, not passing.
justifications.evidence: Every cited log was opened and matches. Both negative controls are well formed and independent, and each first line repeats its declared mutation verbatim: 'NEGATIVE CONTROL: replace the source-selecting expected computation with "expected = archived.get(role, closure.get(role, 0))" and remove the "expected_source" field from each parity row; leave the observed lookup unchanged' ending '2 failed' exit 1, and 'NEGATIVE CONTROL: replace "live = observed.get(identity, {})" with "live = {}" in _archive_role_parity' ending '1 failed' exit 1. They are genuinely independent - one holds observed fixed while mutating expected, the other the reverse - which is the right shape for a change that touches both halves of a row. focused-receipt.log ends '6 passed' exit 0. The suite delta checks arithmetically: baseline at 9a5e40f4b '20 failed, 7497 passed, 8 skipped, 326 deselected ... 3 errors' and after at a19188a6e '20 failed, 7499 passed, 8 skipped, 326 deselected ... 3 errors' - the two 23-element failure id lists are identical and passed moves by exactly the two tests added. Reproduced here at the integrated head: the four archive-reconstruction test files return 40 passed exit 0 (review-focused.log). WHAT THE TWO CONTROLS DO NOT COVER, reported separately as the gate asks. First and most material, neither control perturbs the PRECEDENCE the change's own docstring asserts - archive census first, then closure. Swapping the two branches leaves both controls green, because the landed tests only ever place a role in one source or the other: EVIDENCED_BY is in archived and never in closure, HAS_UNIT is in closure and (in the three-source test) never in archived. Second, neither control touches the refusal loop, so nothing in the suite demonstrates that inverting the refusal to the census would be caught. It would be caught - test_parity_counts_the_loss_of_a_role_with_no_reconstruction_route asserts an APPLIED receipt with census EVIDENCED_BY 2 against live 0, which a census-governed refusal turns red - but that is inference from reading, not a demonstrated control. Third, no log exercises the CLI print path that is the sole consumer of the new null; I ran it here, the node did not.
justifications.fit: The change fits the module. The docstring was rewritten to state the mechanism rather than the old prose, the role iteration keeps the derived union sorted(_ARCHIVE_PARITY_ROLES | set(archived)) so the receipt and the registry cannot drift, and the dict-comprehension-to-explicit-loop conversion is the right call once three branches are needed. It sits correctly beside _archive_role_outcomes and reuses authority.archive_roles rather than re-deriving. Docked twice. First, the return type widened to dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, int | str | None]]], which types a HETEROGENEOUS record as a uniform mapping: it says every value may be a str, so nothing at a call site can narrow role_counts['expected'] to int | None without a cast, and a consumer that wanted to sum a column is now type-correct in doing something nonsensical. A TypedDict with expected: int | None, expected_source: str, observed: int would carry the shape the four tests already assert exactly. Second, SIGNED_MANIFEST_RECEIPT_SCHEMA stays 'imas-codex.signed-repair-receipt.v1' while the parity row went from two fields to three and expected gained null, so the schema string an external reader would key on cannot distinguish the shapes. No in-repo consumer does, which is why this is a dock and not a finding.

The goal is met. In this reviewer's worktree, an apply with archive_roles={} yields 35 parity rows of which HAS_UNIT is {expected 1, expected_source reconstruction_closure, observed 1} and the other 34 are {expected null, expected_source neither, observed 0}; adding archive_roles={EVIDENCED_BY: 2} moves that row to {expected 2, expected_source archive_census, observed 0}. All three sources are therefore distinguishable on real inputs and the fabricated zero is gone. THE THREE FENCED QUESTIONS, each yes or no. The mapping has exactly one non-test consumer, imas_codex/cli/sn.py:8466, and it only interpolates: f"expected {role_counts['expected']} observed {role_counts['observed']}". Executed here against a real None row it prints 'parity archived_temperature HAS_PARENT: expected None observed 0' without raising. No arithmetic, no comparison, no sort on the value anywhere. (2) Does the refusal path still read the reconstruction closure rather than the archive census - YES, and the diff proves it by omission: the only hunk in signed_manifest.py is inside _archive_role_parity, and the refusal loop at 7417-7431 is untouched, still building expected = dict.fromkeys(_ARCHIVE_EDGE_COUNTERPARTS, 0) incremented from authority.edges and comparing live.get(role, 0) over expected.items(). Demonstrated rather than asserted: a live surplus on the reconstructable role HAS_UNIT (extra_counts 5) raises SignedManifestConflict('archive-versus-live relationship counts differ'), while a live surplus of 3 on EVIDENCED_BY applies cleanly and merely shows {expected null, neither, observed 3}. Every migrated assertion is still full-dict equality against a literal, and the exhaustiveness assertion was TIGHTENED from set(counts) == {expected, observed} to {expected, expected_source, observed}; two of the four gained an additional exact-shape assertion they did not previously carry. The only non-assertion edit is renaming a fixture file from authority.json to conflicting-authority.json to avoid a collision with the newly added apply in the same tmp_path.

The plan edit is +3 lines, a single worker-owned r-comment; no meta line and no terminal state touched. Both commits are conventional with real bodies ('fix(standard-names): distinguish receipt expectation sources', 'docs(evidence): record receipt expectation provenance'). A case-insensitive scan of both messages for co-authored-by / generated with / claude / copilot returns 0 hits. No plan, sprint or ticket label appears in any added symbol, filename or comment - the new file is named test_archive_parity_receipt.py and the new field expected_source, both mechanism names.
